transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jonas Meyer (Redwood SE); Priya Khatri (Redwood CSM); Carlos Ruiz (Veridian SRE); Marta Novak (Veridian Platform Eng); Liam O'Connor (Veridian CTO); Anika Bose (Veridian SecOps); Tariq Elm (Veridian Developer)

Summary: Quick follow-up to the escalation last week where we saw a steady cumulative error slope in production. Goal: triage root causes, agree an immediate scaleback runbook, and assign owners for telemetry and security follow-ups.

[00:00] Maya Patel: okay thanks everyone for jumping on, uh, i know time's tight so we'll kick off. main goal here is to lock down an immediate mitigation to stop the error slope and then plan the bench and long-term fixes.
[00:22] Carlos Ruiz: yeah thanks maya. quick context — the slope started about 10 days ago after we pushed a batch-change that increased tail latency for long responses. errors are mostly 5xx timeouts plus some kv-cache misses that cascade.
[00:40] Marta Novak: to add, we also had two large retrain jobs overlap which saturated network egress to our storage, so some requests were queued and then timed out at the app layer. not sure if that's infra or model serving config yet.
[01:05] Jonas Meyer: okay, so two orthogonal things — backpressure from upstream batch jobs and then cache cold-starts. both can manifest as a slow build in error rate rather than a big spike. that matches the slope.
[01:28] Anika Bose: security note, some of the long jobs touch PII feature tables, so we need to keep the VPC and KMS context in any mitigation plan — can't just move to a shared cache without a compliance check.
[01:45] Priya Khatri: good flag, anika. we'll include that in the runbook, and i'll also attach the SOC2 sections we referenced previously.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: before we go to mitigations, can we confirm whether this is a Redwood runtime issue vs our infra, or a mix? we need to know where to put engineering effort.
[02:20] Jonas Meyer: brief answer — it's mixed. our telemetry shows increased queuing on the serving layer when the request size distribution skews high. also, the kv cache had a >30% miss rate on longer prompts this week. those two together amplify tail latencies. not a fundamental bug in runtime kernels, more an orchestration + cache priming problem.
[02:50] Carlos Ruiz: we saw the queue depth rise slowly when the long responses started; with autoscale it didn't break but it moved more requests into the longer queue, and our app timeouts kicked in.
[03:10] Maya Patel: okay, so immediate mitigations suggested: 1) scaleback thresholds (reject or re-route the very long requests to a lower-cost async path), 2) prefix/KV prefill for known hot prompts, 3) temporary throttles on non-critical batch jobs. do we agree as a package?
[03:36] Marta Novak: yes but we need specifics. what's the recommended threshold and how abrupt is the scaleback? we don't want to break user flows.
[03:50] Jonas Meyer: recommended conservative start: if average token time > 450ms or request length > 2k tokens, route to async queue or a trimmed model variant. scaleback should be gradual — start with rejecting 5% of the longest requests with 503 and a retry hint, monitor for 24 hours, then widen if needed. we'll provide a helm patch and a script to toggle thresholds.
[04:20] Tariq Elm: is there a way to auto-fallback to a quantized model? we have some use cases where quality drop is acceptable for latency.
[04:32] Jonas Meyer: yes, we can route to a quantized variant with lower latency and cheaper tokens; fallback policies are supported. note: quantization may change logits slightly so evals are recommended for critical prompts.
[04:50] Anika Bose: again, VPC/KMS — if we route to a hosted quantized model we need to ensure keys and logs don't leave the compliance boundary. can Redwood confirm the private deployment option for this?
[05:05] Maya Patel: short answer: yes, Dedicated or Private allows you to keep keys and PVs in your VPC. priya will share the private deployment checklist.
[05:18] Priya Khatri: i'll add that to the follow-up email and include the KMS integration notes.
[05:28] Carlos Ruiz: on telemetry — we need higher-cardinality traces for the KV miss path plus a breakdown by user cohort. current dashboards aggregate too much. can redwood provide a filterable trace export?
[05:45] Jonas Meyer: we can push per-request trace ids and a lightweight playback bundle. i'll include a script to sample the traces and a small lambda to map trace IDs back to request attributes.
[06:05] Marta Novak: great. also, would a prefilling policy keyed on stable user prompts help? we have a small set of hot templates.
[06:17] Jonas Meyer: absolutely — prefix prefill helps a lot. we can pre-populate the KV cache for known hot keys at deploy time and keep TTLs conservative. we'll include a recommended prefill list format in the runbook.
[06:33] Liam O'Connor: procurement question — if we need dedicated pods for peak stability, what is the likely timeline and cost?
[06:44] Maya Patel: quick orientation — Dedicated requires a 30-day lead for pod allocation typically, and we can provide cost estimates based on your current token throughput. i'll coordinate with finance after we get your histograms.
[07:00] Carlos Ruiz: sending histograms now (in chat). expect them in a few minutes.
[07:12] Maya Patel: perfect. action owners then: jonas will produce scaleback script; priya will send security checklist; carlos and marta run benchmark. we'll reconvene after benchmark.
[07:28] Marta Novak: a couple of edge concerns — how do we ensure training jobs don't auto-scale during peak inference windows? our kube cluster autoscaler policies currently treat both the same.
[07:45] Jonas Meyer: two options: node taints for inference nodes, or a pod priority class separation. taints ensure training pods don't schedule on inference nodes; priority classes ensure preemption behavior. preference depends on your ops tolerance.
[08:05] Tariq Elm: would taints interfere with some of our internal CI pipelines?
[08:12] Marta Novak: possibly, but we can carve out a spot. this will need coordination with infra.
[08:22] Anika Bose: security question — what's the log retention and who can access full request bodies for debugging? we need RBAC to be explicit.
[08:34] Priya Khatri: Redwood supports token-level RBAC for logs and full request obfuscation. we'll attach the RBAC guide.
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: good. next, on benchmarks — can Redwood share a minimal benchmark harness we can run inside our VPC to simulate skewed long requests?
[08:56] Jonas Meyer: yes, small GO-based harness and a k8s job that will generate request shape. we'll include instructions for simulating token distributions.
[09:12] Carlos Ruiz: would be helpful to include a 'safe mode' helm chart that flips scaleback on/off without redeploying.
[09:22] Jonas Meyer: agreed — that's the plan for the patch. toggle via configmap or CRD, no full pod restart.
[09:33] Maya Patel: ok, let's capture acceptance criteria for this runbook: 1) error slope reduced to baseline within 24 hours of scaleback activation; 2) no more than 3% increase in 500s for non-affected flows; 3) benchmark reproducible in customer env.
[09:55] Marta Novak: those look reasonable. we'll sign off if the benchmark meets criteria.
[10:08] Liam O'Connor: timeline reminder — procurement for Dedicated might take three weeks, so the benchmark is the gating item for that decision.
[10:20] Priya Khatri: i'll add that to the follow-up timeline.
[10:28] Maya Patel: any other blocker items?
[10:34] Anika Bose: one more — we need that KMS integration diagram for security review board.
[10:41] Priya Khatri: noted, i'll attach diagram and a short note on key rotation policy.
[10:48] Carlos Ruiz: ok, will run benchmark and report back.
[10:55] Maya Patel: great. recap and owners will go out after the call. thanks everyone.

END OF TRANSCRIPT

Notes: transcript has minor transcription errors (speaker overlap, partial words) intentionally to mimic Fireflies exports. References to helm/CRD, KV cache, quantized model, TTLs, VPC, KMS, RBAC, and Dedicated pods were discussed.
